newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on Tuesday due to profit-taking triggered by overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended at an intra-day high of 19,580 yuan ($2,358) per tonne, losing 40 yuan. It opened at 19,400 and hit a low of 19,390.
November fell 170 to 19,080 yuan, December 160 to 19,200, January 40 to 19,500, March 90 to 19,600, April 110 to 19,600 and May 100 to 19,600.
Combined volume fell to 66,260 tonnes from 99,150.
Copper opened lower. Short-covering pushed the prices up from lows but still down from Monday's close.
Traders said long and short position holders liquidated their positions because they perceived bigger risk.

"Many investors felt that the risk was rising, with the contracts approaching the key 20,000-yuan resistance level," one trader said. "They are willing to stay on the sidelines and wait for a clear market trend."
Traders said technical charts indicate there is potential for further rises but no-one knows how far they will go.
"Panic selling did not emerge despite the falls and copper is likely to rise further after a consolidation," a second trader said.
"But I do not know if it can breach the 20,000-yuan level, which it has not hit since early October," he added.
Aluminium ended mixed. November fell 30 to 13,420 yuan per tonne, December rose 60 to 13,420 and January unchanged at 13,400.
Combined volume fell to 430 tonnes from 1,070.
